prompt:
Use case: illustration-story.
Asset type: an interior illustration for the Ukrainian science fiction diary "Повстання Мюридів" in the Дике Поле universe.
Create an original monochrome graphite pencil sketch on clean slightly warm off-white paper, as if the narrator Vasyl Vyhovsky, a veteran officer, hastily sketched the view in his private diary while departing aboard a transport. Adventure-novel illustration sensibility, intimate observational field sketch rather than a polished concept painting.
Scene: oblique downward view through a spacecraft transport window during early ascent above the futuristic capital Zoryana Sich. Below is a huge memorial park of oaks arranged along radial and concentric paths. At the very center stand THREE ancient broad-crowned oaks: the tallest central oak spreads branches protectively over its two neighboring oaks; one neighboring oak is the narrator's ancestral oak and is the emotional focus, slightly more carefully drawn. Surrounding rings of trees recede into sketchy strokes, suggesting thousands of trees rather than depicting each. Tiny simple information kiosks sit by the trees. Beyond the park, a few understated distant futuristic civic buildings, only lightly indicated.
Composition: landscape book vignette, first-person view with only a partial curved spacecraft window rim sketched along one side and lower corner. The memorial grove remains clearly visible during ascent, not an orbital view. The central grove is the strongest area of detail; outer edges dissolve naturally into blank paper, generous blank margins. No visible artist, hands, pencil, desk, open-book mockup or page fold. No prominent portrait reflection.
Medium: visibly authentic graphite pencil, confident but imperfect contours, loose crosshatching, varying pressure, pale construction lines, slight erasures and graphite smudges, a few unfinished forms. Detailed oak branches and organic crown textures, rougher architecture and window. Restrained dark accents, ample white paper. It should feel drawn from a brief personal memory by an observant soldier, not mechanically filtered from a photograph.
Mood: quiet longing, interrupted homecoming, one last glimpse of a tree he never got to visit before duty called.
No text, captions, signature, lettering, watermark, flags or insignia. No blue-and-yellow flag bands, no modern Ukrainian coat of arms, no decorative cloth. No color, ink wash, watercolor, photorealism, 3D render, glossy digital shading, explosions or battle.
